prompt: a phoenix emblem, high contrast woodcut, flat colours, thick closed shapes, pure white background
what_it_proves: the default model at its own distilled schedule (4 steps, guidance 1.0) still makes a trace-ready emblem, so the baseline every other example is compared against is a real run and not a default nobody checked.

prompt: an owl crest, flat heraldic shapes, limited palette of four colours, hard edges, white background
what_it_proves: the undistilled sibling actually runs classifier-free guidance and a negative prompt, which is the one thing the distilled default cannot do.

prompt: remove the background completely, keep the subject unchanged, pure white background
what_it_proves: a LoRA edit on a real reference: the adapter loads, is applied to klein's unified image= path, and the result has one flat background region instead of the gradients a tracer chokes on.

prompt: remove the sword from the emblem, keep everything else identical
what_it_proves: an object-removal adapter on the same model, to show the two klein edit adapters are separately selectable rather than one interchangeable blob.

prompt: extend the image outward into a wider flat background, keep the crest centred and unchanged
what_it_proves: the one adapter whose useful output is a larger canvas than its input, and the only path here that changes the composition rather than the style.

prompt: a 4 by 2 sprite sheet of a phoenix mascot, eight poses on one flat background, hard pixel-free edges, no shading
what_it_proves: the spritesheet adapter as text-to-image: a grid of flat cells with one background colour is the easiest raster in this whole set to trace.

prompt: a minimalist falcon head logo mark inside a circle
what_it_proves: a print style and the adapter it names, together: the style steers the prompt and the LoRA supplies the logo idiom, on the model the style suggests.

prompt: a flat vector wolf head badge, four solid colours, hard edges, white background
what_it_proves: the 4-step Lightning LoRA with the scheduler swap it requires: without the trailing-Euler swap this produces noise, not a cheaper image, so a non-blank frame here is the proof the scheduler was actually installed.

prompt: a flat vector wolf head badge, four solid colours, hard edges, white background
what_it_proves: the 2-step sibling at the same prompt and seed, so the 2-step and 4-step adapters can be compared directly instead of being described as interchangeable.

prompt: a flat vector wolf head badge, four solid colours, hard edges, white background
what_it_proves: the 8-step adapter, closing the three-way comparison at one prompt and one seed — the difference between them is quality, not just wall clock.

prompt: a flat geometric sunburst poster, six solid colours, hard edges, no gradients
what_it_proves: the LCM adapter with LCMScheduler installed — the other scheduler-swapping family, and the one whose guidance must stay at 1.0 because it was trained without CFG.

prompt: a small hero character sprite, front view, single subject
what_it_proves: the only adapter whose card states its own schedule (8 steps, guidance 1.5) — so this example also proves the registry's numbers came from the card and not from a guess.

prompt: layered paper cut art of a mountain range and a sun, solid colour shapes, visible occlusion edges
what_it_proves: the largest style adapter (340 MB, full-rank) under a style that names no model or adapter, so it also covers the plain 'style plus your own choices' path.

prompt: a flat vector lighthouse badge, five solid colours, hard edges, white background
what_it_proves: a VAE swap at a real size: byte-for-byte the same decoder as SDXL's, so a non-blank frame proves the swap's ORDERING — a VAE assigned after the offload map was built fails inside the scheduler step with a device mismatch.

prompt: a flat vector lighthouse badge, five solid colours, hard edges, white background
what_it_proves: the tiny autoencoder (AutoencoderTiny, not a smaller AutoencoderKL) at the same prompt as the fp16-fix example, so its visibly softer decode is a comparison someone can look at rather than a claim.

prompt: a flat geometric fox head, four solid colours, hard edges, white background
what_it_proves: the fastest entry in the registry also runs — but it is non-commercial, so running this example requires CHOPSHOP_FLUX_ACK_NONCOMMERCIAL=1 and its output may not be sold. That is the point: the cheapest generation is the one you may not use.

prompt: a flat vector mushroom badge, four solid colours, thick outline, white background
what_it_proves: the smallest model in the registry with its own LCM adapter, on the one target that adapter supports — a 0.86B model at 4 steps is the cheapest commercially usable run here.

prompt: a flat vector mushroom badge, four solid colours, thick outline, white background
what_it_proves: the SD 1.5 fine-tuned MSE VAE on its own model — the swap that changes how smooth the flat areas are, which is exactly what a tracer sees.

prompt: a flat vector mushroom badge, four solid colours, thick outline, white background
what_it_proves: the SD 1.5 tiny VAE, to show the same 30x size cut on the small model — and to see the softness land on the outlines a tracer depends on.

prompt: a flat vector bee emblem, five solid colours, hard edges, white background, no gradients
what_it_proves: a whole second architecture at 2 steps: Sana Sprint is guidance-embedded rather than CFG-distilled, so guidance 4.5 is honoured here in a way it never is on klein — and its first call after a load is slow while the second is fast, which is why both numbers are reported.

prompt: a flat vector bee emblem, five solid colours, hard edges, white background, no gradients
what_it_proves: the 1.6B Sana at the same prompt and seed as the 0.6B, so the extra 3.2 GB of transformer is compared rather than described.

prompt: a cheerful cartoon fox head
what_it_proves: SSD-1B running SDXL's own pipeline class and an SDXL style adapter, which is the cheapest way to get an SDXL-shaped result — its step and guidance numbers are estimates, and this run is what would confirm or contradict them.

prompt: a friendly cartoon owl perched on a branch
what_it_proves: outline art with unfilled white regions — the closest thing in this set to a raster a tracer can follow without a colour-quantisation step.

prompt: flatten to pure black outlines on white, no fills, uniform line weight
what_it_proves: an SD-style img2img edit with a strength, on a family whose edit path is a DIFFERENT class (StableDiffusionXLImg2ImgPipeline) with an adapter loaded onto it.

prompt: a flat vector cat silhouette, three solid colours, hard edges, white background
what_it_proves: the original SDXL VAE swapped onto SSD-1B, which is both the way back after a swap and the control for comparing every other decode against the one the pipeline shipped with.

prompt: a geometric mountain range poster with a sun, limited palette
what_it_proves: a print style whose suffix alone does the work on the default model — no adapter, no model change, so it isolates what the style text contributes.

prompt: a heraldic crest of a stag and oak leaves, inked outline
what_it_proves: the line-art style with no adapter at all, to separate the style's contribution from every adapter in this set.
